claim: More than 225,000 people dead, 225,000. The estimates are, if we’d have acted responsibly, there’d be 160,000 fewer dead than there are today, because of covid-19.
justification: The claim's assertion of over 225,000 COVID-19 deaths by October 30, 2020, is contradicted by evidence assessments indicating the verified death toll was approximately 212,000, as seen in the low-confidence evidence items that are discounted. Additionally, the claim of 160,000 fewer deaths with responsible action is refuted by high-confidence evidence (confidence 0.90) stating there is no credible support for this figure and that the underlying study was corrected, rendering the claim unsupported.
